git-explain-welcome: Welcome to GitExplain — your interactive Git command sandbox!
git-explain-summary: Learn, test, and master Git directly in your browser!
git-init-first-step: Creates a hidden .git folder in the current directory.
git-init-second-step: Initializes a new Git repository, which can be used for versioning code.
git-init-third-step: Sets up the local repository, allowing you to start tracking changes and creating commits.
git-init-fourth-step: If the repository is already initialized, the command does not overwrite it but simply confirms that the repository already exists.
git-init-quiet-option: -q/--quiet = Only prints error or warning messages. All other output is suppressed.
git-init-bare-option: --bare = Creates a bare repository. If the GIT_DIR environment variable is not set, it defaults to the current working directory.
